title: Data Quality in RVL-CDIP: A Systematic Audit
abstract: arXiv:2610.32126v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: RVL-CDIP is the de facto standard benchmark for document classification, and reported accuracy on it is now 98.8%. In this paper, we audit RVL-CDIP for data quality issues and find that approximately 10.5% of its 400,000 documents have erroneous labels and that 35.2% of the test set has a duplicate or near-duplicate in the training set. Identification codes on the pages are sufficient to classify at 69% accuracy, and a state-of-the-art model loses 11 points without them. Image-only models trained on RVL-CDIP lose 16 to 28 points on documents from other sources, and the choice of OCR engine changes accuracy by 4.1 to 8.3 points. We find that nearly 16,000 RVL-CDIP documents contain sensitive personal data, and produce de-identified versions of these documents. translated_title: RVL-CDIP中的数据质量：一项系统性审计

tldr: 本文对文档分类标准基准RVL-CDIP进行了系统性数据质量审计，发现约10.5%的标签错误和35.2%的训练-测试集重复问题，并在修复缺陷后重新基准测试25个模型，显示重训练模型准确率可提升0.9至2.9个百分点。
en_tdlr: This paper systematically audits the RVL-CDIP document classification benchmark, revealing ~10.5% label errors and 35.2% train-test duplication, and demonstrates that retrained models improve accuracy by 0.9 to 2.9 points after remediation.
